description:
We are the Martians, a team of 6 space enthusiasts participating in our first NASA Space Apps Challenge! We are beginners at coding but bring strong skills in research, creative writing, and multimedia design. 

We are looking to tackle a beginner-friendly project focused on Mars, planetary exploration, or educational storytelling. 

Our team is currently open to welcoming new members
summary: ARES (Advanced Rover Exploration System) is a mission-control web app that answers a simple question: where on Mars is it worth going, and is the way there passable? Terrain, weather and science results usually live in separate archives and tools, so ARES brings them together in one interface. Users explore an interactive 3D Mars globe with landing sites and discoveries, inspect terrain through elevation, slope and hazard maps, and plan rover routes with an A* planner that compares direct, balanced and cautious paths by distance, slope and hazard. A mission dashboard summarizes the selected location, route difficulty, environmental readings and scientific points of interest, and an assistant answers questions using project data. Every value is labeled live, historical or simulated, so the tool never presents demonstration data as a real observation.
details:
The problem: Crews and mission planners need terrain, weather and science information together to decide where to explore, but these live in separate archives and tools.

What ARES does:

  • Mars Explorer: an interactive 3D globe with landing sites (such as Jezero, Gale and Olympus Mons) and scientific discoveries.
  • Terrain Analysis: elevation, slope and hazard maps; clicking any point shows its values.
  • Route Planner: A* routes between two sites, compared as Direct, Balanced and Cautious by distance, slope and hazard.
  • Discovery Explorer: science points of interest filtered by category, such as ancient water, minerals and habitability.
  • Environment: temperature, pressure and wind readings, each labeled live, historical or simulated.
  • Mission Dashboard and ARES Assistant: one view of location, route difficulty and nearby science sites, plus an assistant that answers from project data and never claims a route is safe.

Data and honesty: ARES is built around NASA’s Planetary Data System and NASA Trek (Mars), with Mars Odyssey, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express as reference sources. Where live data wasn’t available, such as the terrain model and weather endpoint, the app uses demonstration data and labels it SIMULATED.

Tools & Technologies:

  • Languages: JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3
  • Frontend: React.js, Tailwind CSS, Bootstrap
  • Backend: Node.js, Express.js
  • Database: MongoDB
  • Libraries: Axios, React Router, Mongoose
  • Tools: Git, GitHub, VS Code, Postman

Impact and creativity: ARES turns scattered Mars data into a single decision-support view and treats data trust as a feature, so users always know what is real and what is simulated.
